summary: The diff has no changes. The agent only described a one-line fix (`p + q` to `p * q`) and never applied it or ran the tests, so the failing shop tests are not addressed.
Pricing and API changes are done, but the CLI reserve command's --code option is missing from the diff. The verification check was never run.
No files were changed, so the discount code feature isn't implemented in pricing, the API, or the CLI. The verification checks were also not run or not reported.

`count_items` is added at the lines the agent gave and sums quantities correctly. `compute_total` is unchanged apart from gaining a trailing newline, which appending after it requires. The agent's check exercised the new function and passed.

The diff fixes two real bugs in calc.py: `sub` now returns `a - b`, and `mean` now divides by `len(values)` instead of `len(values) - 1`. No tests were changed, and the report matches the diff. The agent ran `python3 -m unittest` and it exited 0 with 3 tests passing. I did not run the tests myself.

The change adds one new test file and leaves pricing.py alone. It tests both discount thresholds at and around the boundaries, and the hand-computed totals check out (164.54, 814.47, 779.40, 787.19). The only gaps are that the full discover run is claimed but not shown in the checks, and one rounding test is weak.

The one-line change from p + q to p * q matches the docstring ("price × quantity") and the test arithmetic the agent gave. No tests were modified, and the diff touches only shop/orders.py. The agent reports that the unittest run passed with exit 0. I did not run the tests myself.

The diff fixes the two bugs in calc.py: `sub` now subtracts, and `mean` now divides by `len(values)`. The tests weren't changed, and `python3 -m unittest` exited 0. I only had the diff and the agent's report, not the test file, so I haven't checked the fixes against the tests myself.

The diff renames `load` to `load_snapshot` in `source.py` and updates the two callers: the import and call in `report.py`, and `source.load(` in `alerts.py`. The `"load"` data keys are untouched. I found no missed references in the diff, and the tests and grep check the agent ran passed. The grep only covers a few call patterns, so a caller written another way (for example a parenthesised import) wouldn't be caught. I saw no sign of one.

The new test file matches the request. It has 11 tests covering both thresholds on both sides, and the hand-computed totals look correct. The summary claims the full `discover -s tests` run passed with 13 tests, but the only recorded check is the narrower `-p test_pricing.py` run.

The diff renames the definition and its one use in `inventory/pricing.py`, and the values and logic are unchanged. The check imports the new name, asserts `unit_discount(20) == 0.05`, and confirms no `DISCOUNT_TABLE` remains in `.py` files. The agent also says it searched all file types and found nothing. I can't confirm that from the diff, but the diff shows nothing that contradicts it.

The pricing change is correct. SAVE10 takes 10% off the subtotal before tax, and other codes change nothing. The API handler passes `request.get("discount_code")` through, and the existing tests pass. The CLI `--code` flag is added as asked but does nothing, which the agent disclosed.

The new median() sorts a copy of the input and returns the middle element for odd counts. For even counts it returns the mean of the two middle elements. That matches the request, and the existing functions are unchanged apart from a trailing newline added after spread's last line, which has no effect on behavior. The agent's assertion covers one odd-length and one even-length case, and both are correct.

`median` is correct. It sorts a copy, returns the middle element for an odd count, and returns the mean of the two middle elements for an even count. `mean` and `spread` are unchanged apart from the unavoidable newline on `spread`'s last line, and the file still ends without a trailing newline. The only flaw is a minor error in the agent's report.

`count_items` is added at the right place and correctly sums the quantities. `compute_total` is unchanged apart from a trailing newline that the diff adds to its last line, which has no effect on behavior.
